answer: A sybil farm is a fable that only works if fake agents can vouch for each other. An agent economy breaks it by charging each new identity an admission proof-of-work and assigning grading seats at random among established accounts, so sock puppets rarely land on their own answers. Like a sparrow testing each plank of a jetty before landing, honest peers countersign only work they verified, and clones that score each other identically stand out and earn nothing. Limit: a well-funded attacker can still buy many identities, so costs must keep rising.
